notes.md: - **Interim Budget 2019-20:** presented by **Piyush Goyal** on **1 Feb 2019**; set out a **'Vision 2030'** with **ten dimensions**, the first being physical and social infrastructure for a **USD 10 trillion** economy and ease of living.

- **JPC chairmen:** Bofors (1987) – **B. Shankaranand**; Harshad Mehta scam (1992) – **Ram Niwas Mirdha**; Ketan Parekh scam (2001) – **Lt Gen Prakash Mani Tripathi** (retd); soft-drink pesticides (2003) – **Sharad Pawar**; 2G spectrum (2011) – **P.C. Chacko**.

- **Collective privileges** (of the House): publish its debates and stop others publishing them; **exclude strangers** and hold secret sittings; receive **immediate information of a member's arrest**, detention or release; make its own rules; punish members and outsiders for breach or contempt.
- **Individual privileges** (of members): freedom of speech; freedom from arrest in **civil cases** (40 days before and after a session); **exemption from jury service**; may decline to give evidence in a court while the House is in session.

- **Cost of disruption:** in **2012** the Parliamentary Affairs Minister (**Pawan Kumar Bansal**) put the cost of running Parliament at about **Rs 2.5 lakh per minute**; this figure is still used to value time lost to disruptions.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides that the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses?
new.x: Article 118(4) says the Speaker presides over a joint sitting; Article 108 only provides for summoning it.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: Art. 118(4) Speaker presides joint sitting

new.s: A Constitutional Amendment Bill that changes the federal provisions must be ratified by how many State Legislatures?
new.x: Under Article 368, an amendment of federal provisions also needs ratification by the legislatures of half of the States.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: CA bill - State ratification half the States

new.s:
Consider the following statements about a Constitutional Amendment Bill under Article 368:
1. It must be passed in each House separately by a special majority.
2. If it affects federal provisions, it must be ratified by half of the States.
3. A deadlock between the two Houses on it can be settled at a joint sitting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It needs a special majority in each House and ratification by half the States for federal provisions; there is no joint sitting for such a Bill.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: CA bill - special majority, State ratification, no joint sitting

new.s: Which Bill, giving effect to the tax proposals of the Budget, is usually certified by the Speaker as a Money Bill?
new.x: The Finance Bill puts the Budget's tax proposals into effect and is usually certified as a Money Bill.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: Finance Bill usually certified as Money Bill

new.s: In the Monsoon Session of 2026, which Bill was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
new.x: The FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was referred to a JPC in the Monsoon Session 2026, after a push by the united opposition.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: Monsoon 2026 - FCRA (Amendment) Bill to JPC

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for summoning a joint sitting under Article 108?
o: The other House rejects the Bill
The two Houses finally disagree on amendments to the Bill
More than six months pass without the other House passing the Bill
The other House does not return the Bill within 14 days
new.x: The three grounds are rejection, final disagreement on amendments, and six months' delay; the 14-day limit applies only to Money Bills, which never go to a joint sitting.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: joint sitting grounds

new.s: Which committee of the Lok Sabha examines Private Members' Bills seeking to amend the Constitution before they are introduced?
o: Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions
new.x: In the Lok Sabha, the Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions classifies such Bills, allots time and examines private members' constitutional amendment Bills before introduction.
new.angle: U0307 notes gap: Committee on PMBs examines CA bills

new.s: Since which year had India a separate Railway Budget before it was merged with the Union Budget in 2017?
new.x: The separate Railway Budget began in 1924 and ended with its merger into the Union Budget in 2017.
new.angle: U0308 notes gap: separate Railway Budget since 1924

new.s: From which year has the Union Budget been presented on 1 February?
new.x: The Budget date was moved to 1 February from 2017; Arun Jaitley presented the first such combined Budget on 1 February 2017.
new.angle: U0308 notes gap: Budget date 1 February from 2017

new.s: Who presented the separate agriculture budget of Andhra Pradesh for 2026-27?
new.x: Payyavula Keshav presented the AP Budget 2026-27 on 14 February 2026, and K. Atchannaidu presented the separate agriculture budget.
new.angle: U0308 notes gap: AP agriculture budget 2026-27 - K. Atchannaidu

new.s: From which fund are the emoluments of the Governor of a State paid?
new.x: Under Article 158(3), the Governor's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.
new.angle: U0308 notes gap: Governor's emoluments - State fund, charged

new.s: When one person is Governor of two or more States, who decides the share of his emoluments to be paid by each State?
o: The Chief Ministers of those States jointly
new.x: Article 158(3A) says the emoluments are shared among the States in the proportion the President fixes by order.
new.angle: U0308 notes gap: Art. 158(3A) one Governor for two States

new.s: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the emoluments, allowances and privileges of the President, Governors, judges and the CAG?
new.x: The Second Schedule deals with emoluments, allowances and privileges; the Third Schedule has the forms of oaths.
new.angle: U0308 notes gap: Second Schedule - emoluments

new.s: Who presented the Interim Union Budget 2019-20, which set out a 'Vision 2030' with ten dimensions?
new.x: Piyush Goyal presented the Interim Budget on 1 February 2019 and laid out ten dimensions of Vision 2030.
new.angle: U0308 web fact: Interim Budget 2019 Vision 2030 - presenter

new.s: The first dimension of 'Vision 2030' in the Interim Union Budget 2019-20 aimed at infrastructure for an economy of what size?
new.x: The first dimension was to build physical and social infrastructure for a USD 10 trillion economy and to provide ease of living.
new.angle: U0308 web fact: Vision 2030 - USD 10 trillion economy

new.s: How many members does the Committee on Public Undertakings have?
o: 22: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
31: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
new.x: Like the PAC, the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
new.angle: U0309 notes gap: COPU strength 22 (15+7)

new.s:
Match the following:
List-I (Committee)
A. Estimates Committee
B. Public Accounts Committee
C. Committee on Public Undertakings
D. Each Departmentally Related Standing Committee
List-II (Strength)
1. 22, with an Opposition chairman by convention
2. 31
3. 30, all from the Lok Sabha
4. 22, chairman chosen from its Lok Sabha members
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
new.x: Estimates has 30 (all LS); PAC and COPU have 22 each, PAC chaired by the Opposition and COPU's chairman taken from its LS members; each DRSC has 31.
new.angle: U0309 notes gap: COPU strength and chairman

new.s: The Departmentally Related Standing Committees began with 17 committees in 1993. Since which year have there been 24?
new.x: The DRSC system started with 17 committees in 1993 and was enlarged to 24 committees in 2004.

new.s: Which of the following is an ad hoc inquiry committee of Parliament?
new.x: The Railway Convention Committee, like the committees on MPLADS and Security in Parliament Complex, is an ad hoc inquiry committee; the others are standing committees.
new.angle: U0309 notes gap: ad hoc inquiry committees - Railway Convention

new.s: Who was the chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Bofors issue (1987)?
new.x: Congress leader B. Shankaranand chaired the 1987 JPC on Bofors; it reported in April 1988.
new.angle: U0309 web fact: Bofors JPC chairman

new.s: Within how many days may a political party condone a member's vote against its whip, so that the member is not disqualified?
new.x: Under the Tenth Schedule, a member who votes or abstains against the whip is not disqualified if the party condones it within 15 days.
new.angle: U0310 notes gap: condonation within 15 days

new.s: Which body recommended deleting both the split and the merger exceptions of the Tenth Schedule and treating pre-poll alliances as parties?
new.x: The Law Commission's 170th Report (1999) recommended deleting the split and merger provisions and treating pre-poll alliances as parties.
new.angle: U0310 notes gap: Law Commission 170th - delete split and merger

new.s: Which of the following is a collective privilege of a House of Parliament, and not an individual privilege of its members?
o: Freedom from arrest in civil cases
Right to receive immediate information of the arrest of a member
Right to decline to give evidence in a court while the House is in session
new.x: The right to be informed at once of a member's arrest, detention or release belongs to the House; the other three are privileges of individual members.
new.angle: U0310 web fact: collective vs individual privileges

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an individual privilege of a Member of Parliament?
o: Freedom of speech in the House
Freedom from arrest in civil cases during a session
Right to exclude strangers from the sittings of the House
new.x: Excluding strangers from its sittings is a collective privilege of the House; the others are privileges of individual members.
new.angle: U0310 web fact: collective vs individual privileges

new.s: Which Constitution Amendment Bill proposes to raise the strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850?
new.x: The 131st Amendment Bill proposes a Lok Sabha of 850, changing the Lok Sabha to Rajya Sabha ratio from 2.2:1 to 3.3:1.
new.angle: U0311 notes gap: 131st Amendment Bill - LS 850

new.s: As per the PRS Review of State Laws 2025, which State Assembly met for the fewest days?
new.x: Assemblies met on average for 24 days; Odisha met the most (43) and Nagaland the fewest (7).
new.angle: U0311 notes gap: PRS State laws 2025 - Nagaland 7 days

new.s: What was the theme of the 86th All India Presiding Officers' Conference held at Lucknow?
new.x: The 86th AIPOC at Lucknow had the theme 'Strong Legislature - Prosperous Nation'.
new.angle: U0311 notes gap: 86th AIPOC theme

new.s: In 2012 the Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister put the cost of running Parliament at about how much per minute?
new.x: In 2012 Pawan Kumar Bansal said each minute of Parliament costs about Rs 2.5 lakh; this figure is still used to value time lost to disruptions.
new.angle: U0311 web fact: cost of disruption Rs 2.5 lakh per minute

new.s: By which other names is the parliamentary form of government also known?
new.x: The parliamentary system is also called cabinet government or responsible government, since it stays in power only while it has a majority in the popular House.
new.angle: U0312 notes gap: also called cabinet / responsible government

new.s: Which of the following features is found in the British system but not in the Indian system?
o: Collective responsibility to the lower House
Prime Minister as leader of the majority party
new.x: In Britain ministers are legally responsible (a minister must countersign acts of the Crown); India has no such legal responsibility of ministers.
new.angle: U0312 notes gap: legal responsibility of ministers - Britain only

new.s: Because of its wide power of judicial review, which country's Supreme Court has been called a 'third chamber' of the legislature?
new.x: The US Supreme Court uses 'due process of law' and has wide judicial review, so it is called a 'third chamber'.
new.angle: U0312 notes gap: US Supreme Court - third chamber
